Native text is readable; original title page and contents inspected. Examples/charts/diagrams are retained in the original PDF; column reading order and soft hyphens in extraction can be imperfect. mehen.evidence: Six-page Tabletopia-hosted English Mehen reference with simple and complex playable modern reconstructions; full text read. It explicitly says original ancient rules cannot be recovered. Simple version: six pawns/lion per player, tail-to-head race, throwing-stick values, accumulated throws, capture/re-entry, stacking and lion rules, all pawns safe at the head wins. Complex version adds stored ones, return journey, faster lions and capture-count ending; its introductory all-pawns statement and numbered first-returning-pawn lion trigger disagree, so consult that variant critically. Dice face values are diagrammatic on page 3; use original PDF. Awkward English and speculative historical claims are not certified by recovery. These are named reconstructions, not authenticated ancient rules or a complete summary audit.

alemungula.evidence: igGameCenter’s complete named Ethiopian Wetawit Alemungula rules: two rows of five holes, five seeds per hole, direction chosen by starting-hole location, single sowing skipping stores, 2/4 captures backwards, singleton immediate-return restriction, no-legal-move ending/sweep and most-seed win. Raw served HTML retained unchanged; explicit #gameRules section excludes account/navigation/statistics. Readable English, not an original ethnographic paper or a summary audit.

hyena-chase.evidence: Board and Pieces historical-game reference for Li’b el Marafib/Hyena Chase, using three binary casting dice and accumulated tâba credits, not the simplified six-sided-die variant. Four players, spiral village/well route, exact arrival, four-credit return, winning mother releases a double-speed hyena, two-credit entry/ten-credit drinking and capture by overtaking on its return. Full reference text read; throwing chart and board are image-based in the original live page (HTML preserves references rather than offline image copies). Specific regional rules do not establish errors in a different reconstruction. Summary not audited.

brax.evidence: João Pedro Neto’s May 2025 Brax reference for Frederic Denham’s colored-line capture game, not a different same-title game: seven starting pieces, own-color two-step/enemy-color one-step moves, replacement captures, optional braxing, one-versus-two braxing limitation and lone-piece draw after five captureless turns. Board illustrations and link to original US406632 patent retained in original HTML; English paragraph read in full. Basic two-player game is usable; three/four-player star pieces are mentioned without full variant rules, and braxing details differ among later descriptions. No summary audit.

canadian-checkers.evidence: BrainKing explicitly defines Canadian Checkers as International Checkers on a 12×12 board with 30 pieces per player. This extraction assembles that Canadian section, its linked International rules, and only the linked basic Checkers object-of-game paragraph. International rules override generic English-checkers movement/promotion rules; those contradictory generic rules are excluded. Includes flying kings, backward man captures, maximum capture, removal after full jump, promotion timing and capture-all/immobility victory. Raw Canadian HTML and both linked originals preserved with hashes; starting-position diagrams remain image references. Not a full tournament/draw-code reference or summary audit.

layli-goobalay.evidence: Ralf Gering, Layli Goobalay: The preferred game of the camels, Abstract Games issue 13, Spring 2003, printed page 9 (PDF page 11), with literature/endgame continuation on printed page 14 (PDF page 16, right column only). Marin/Jama-sourced rules explicitly recognize 2×6 and 2×8 boards but illustrate 2×12 with four balls per hole. Regional clockwise and anticlockwise sowing are distinguished. Main setup, relay sowing, capturing, paired Uur holes, inability-to-move ending and repeating-position split are fully present. These rules are a documented regional interpretation, not a claim of one universal variant. Original magazine unchanged; canonical text selects only this article, reading the two columns separately to avoid interleaving; original diagrams remain authoritative. No summary audit.

mangala.evidence: Original-language Turkish modern 48-stone/2×6 Mangala rules from Ata Sporları Federasyonu, supported by Viranşehir district education authority’s November 2024 tournament PDF pages 3–5 (Mangala section only). Federation page supplies four-seed setup and majority victory; tournament rules explicitly supply skipping the opponent’s treasury, single-stone movement, 2/4/6/etc. captures, empty-own/opposite capture and end sweep awarded to the player whose row emptied. Directions are described inconsistently as right/left in the federation prose; tournament PDF explicitly says counterclockwise toward the own treasury. This is modern Turkish Mangala, not the earlier Bedouin/Greek/historic five-seed regional variants. Original HTML/PDF retained; selected text remains Turkish without an invented translation; source-specific match/touch/clock rules are preserved. No summary audit.

chapayev.evidence: Wikipedia contributors, Chapayev (game), CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/, revision 1297880886 linked by the fetched page; retrieved 2026-11-05. Connected-reader HTML snapshot, not raw served HTML. Selected Equipment and Rules sections only. Complete basic regional flicking-checkers game: eight checkers per side, opposing back rows, successful capture without own-piece loss grants another flick, all opposing pieces removed wins round, successive row advancement/retreat, flipped traitors and final-row game end. Article explicitly warns it needs more citations; this is an attributed community rules reference, not publisher authority or a summary audit. Later horse/tank and scissors variants are excluded.
